newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-TOP TEAMS CAN'T AFFORD EARLY SLIPS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-TOP TEAMS CAN'T AFFORD EARLY SLIPS.

text.p: The Czech Republic open the defence of their ice hockey world championship crown on Saturday when they face off against Germany in a pivotal match.
A new format, with six teams instead of eight advancing to the medal round, means there will be no easing into the competition for the medal contenders.
Traditionally teams could recover from an early stumble during round-robin action but that will not be the case this year.

"If you finish fourth in your pool you don't make the medal round," said Canadian coach Andy Murray, whose team will open up against Norway. "It's a much tougher format. There's not room for many mistakes."
Since capturing gold in Vienna last year the Czechs have fallen on hard times, culminating with an embarrassing 7-1 loss to Germany in the quarter-finals of the World Cup last September.

Dissent among players, coaches and officials forced the resignation of Ludek Bukac, the man who guided them to their first world title. He was replaced by ex-NHL player Ivan Hlinka and ex-Calgary Flames assistant Slavomir Lener.
Under the new leadership the Czechs appear to have been undergoing a renaissance amd beat Germany 4-2 and 2-0 in a pair of friendlies leading up to the championship.
"The World Cup was a special circumstance but they knocked us out in Vienna last year," German coach George Kingston said.
"The Czechs have gone through a coaching change but are starting to put things together. But we're quite realistic about our medal chances.
"We want to finish in the top eight but that will mean beating teams like Slovakia, France and maybe the Czechs, so we have our work cut for us."
Finland are hoping to add flashy Montreal Canadiens centre Saku Koviu to their line-up in time for their opening match against France.

But the Finns will have to wait until at least Tuesday before Koivu, who had 17 goals and 56 points for the Canadiens this season, can join them after Montreal avoided elimination from the first round of the Stanley Cup play-offs with a win over New Jersey on Thursday.

Playing at home in front of what is expected to be a sell-out crowd of 14,000 at the brand new Hartwall Arena, Finland are unlikely to need Koivu's help against a French team which will be fighting to avoid relegation.
In pool B action down the coast in Turku, Canada will take on Norway while Sweden face Italy.
The Canadians, ranked as joint-favourites along with Finland, are approaching their match against the Norwegians with caution.
At last year's championship, Norway were the only team to take a point from the Czech Republic, drawing 1-1. They followed up the next night by holding defending champions Finland 2-2.
"There's no easing into this tournament," said Murray. "Norway have been preparing for this game for three weeks and I'm sure they're going to give us all we can handle.
"This is the youngest team Canada has ever sent here and our success could depend on how quickly our players can adjust."
Like Finland, Canada are waiting for more reinforcements from the NHL.
Murray has left one space open on his 23-man roster and said he could make room for further additions by dropping two or three of the players already with the team.
"Those players who might be dropped know who they are because those were the conditions we made when we brought them over," Murray said. "Let's just say we're watching the play-offs very carefully."
The United States will begin their quest for their first world championship title in 64 years on Sunday against Latvia, while Russia open up against Slovakia.
